First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨\frac{4}{t+1}\,,3\sqrt{t}⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\frac{4}{t+1}\,,3\sqrt{t}⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int \frac{4}{t+1}\,\text{d}t,\int 3\sqrt{t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)+{c}_{1},\,2{t}^{\frac{3}{2}}+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The initial condition $F(0)=⟨2,\,-1⟩$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(0)=⟨4\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+{c}_{1},\,2(0)^{\frac{3}{2}}+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\,-1⟩ \\ ⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=2$ and ${c}_{2}=-1.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)+2,\,2{t}^{3/2}-1⟩.
$$
